problem: Existing VLN benchmarks assume instructions perfectly match the environment, but real users' instructions can be outdated because scenes change (blocked paths, removed landmarks, wrong directions), and SOTA agents are not evaluated on this mismatch.
motivation: Human users' understanding of a scene may not be up to date due to instant environment changes, so instructions often deviate slightly from what is navigable. Robust real-world VLN requires agents to cope with imperfectly aligned instruction-environment pairs.
key_idea: Introduce the ImperfectVLN task/dataset (VLN-ChEnv) covering navigability change, incorrect landmark references and incorrect direction descriptions, and add a reflection module that lets the agent review its history to identify errors.
insight: From the abstract: SOTA models show significant performance fluctuations under referred-landmark removal and original-path blockage, indicating reliance on perfectly aligned instructions. A reflection module that reviews history to find errors improves ImperfectVLN performance by 4.4%. Full details are unavailable since only the abstract was provided.
method: ImperfectVLN task/dataset: benchmark for evaluating navigation when instructions and environments are imperfectly matched.
Three modification scenarios: change of navigability (e.g. path blockage), incorrect landmark references (e.g. landmark removal), and incorrect direction descriptions.
Reflection module: lets the agent review its navigation history and identify potential errors, based on the analysis insights.
